payload.instruction: Put a frog in the toilet

program.instruction: Put a frog in the toilet
program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

requirements.text: Put a frog in the toilet
requirements.source_phrase: Put a frog in the toilet

outcomes.description: Add a frog inside the toilet.
outcomes.target: A frog is visibly placed within the toilet bowl.
outcomes.reference: The toilet in the input image.

nodes.question: Compared with the source image, has the requested change—putting a frog in the toilet—made progress, and is that requested change complete?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the edited image visibly shows at least one frog inside the toilet bowl, satisfying the requested placement. Fail if the edited image clearly shows no progress toward placing a frog in the toilet. Do not mark the requested change partial or incomplete solely because additional frogs appear elsewhere; the instruction specifies neither a count nor an exclusion of other placements. Unknown if the images do not provide enough evidence to determine whether a frog is inside the bowl, or if there is a specific visible ambiguity that prevents deciding whether the requested placement is satisfied.
nodes.binding: Compare the source and edited images. Use the toilet in the source image to identify its bowl, and assess whether a visible frog is placed inside that bowl. Treat frogs on the raised lid or floor as additional placements, not by themselves as evidence that the requested bowl placement is incomplete.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

d1: The binding and criteria correctly identify the bowl as the target, but the trace’s confident “yes” treats any visible bowl placement as proof the requested change is complete. In the source, a small dark object is already inside the bowl; in the edit, a frog is clearly added there, so progress is evident. However, the edit also places frogs on the raised lid and floor, and the instruction/rubric define “yes” as all requested changes complete and “partial” as progress without complete fulfillment. The node does not establish whether those extra placements are unrelated edits or affect completion, so its binary pass criterion cannot support the aggregate label. Clarify how to assess completion against the full instruction and rubric, distinguish requested progress from unrelated additions, and allow unresolved status when the images do not establish that distinction. Do not infer incompletion merely from extra frogs; the trace’s visual evidence is strong, and there are no transport, schema, or dependency failures.

observations.evidence: The edited image visibly shows a frog inside the toilet bowl. Other frogs appear on the raised lid and floor, but those additional placements do not negate the bowl placement.
